title: Public baseline paragraph 01
text: A double-entry ledger records every transaction as a debit in one account and a matching credit in another, so the books always balance.

title: Public baseline paragraph 02
text: Append-only ledgers never overwrite past entries; corrections are written as new reversing entries that reference the original.

title: Public baseline paragraph 03
text: Distributed databases often replicate each write to a majority of nodes before acknowledging it to the client.

title: Public baseline paragraph 04
text: Leader election lets a cluster pick one node to coordinate writes; if the leader fails, the remaining nodes elect a replacement.

title: Public baseline paragraph 05
text: Sharding splits a large table across several machines by key range or by hash so that no single server holds all the data.

title: Public baseline paragraph 06
text: Write-ahead logging stores each change durably before it is applied, which allows a database to recover after a crash.

title: Public baseline paragraph 07
text: An on-call rotation assigns engineers to respond to production alerts outside business hours, usually for one week at a time.

title: Public baseline paragraph 08
text: Good incident response starts with a clear severity scale, a named incident commander and a shared status channel.

title: Public baseline paragraph 09
text: Runbooks describe step-by-step actions for common alerts so that responders do not have to improvise at three in the morning.

title: Public baseline paragraph 10
text: Blameless postmortems focus on system and process causes rather than on individual mistakes.

title: Public baseline paragraph 11
text: Alert fatigue happens when pages fire too often for issues that need no action; teams should tune or delete noisy alerts.

title: Public baseline paragraph 12
text: Follow-the-sun support hands tickets between regional teams so that customers get help around the clock.

title: Public baseline paragraph 13
text: REST APIs expose resources at stable URLs and use HTTP verbs such as GET, POST, PUT and DELETE to act on them.

title: Public baseline paragraph 14
text: API versioning, for example a /v1 or /v2 path prefix, lets providers change behaviour without breaking existing clients.

title: Public baseline paragraph 15
text: Idempotency keys allow a client to retry a POST request safely without creating duplicate records.

title: Public baseline paragraph 16
text: Rate limiting protects an API by capping how many requests a client can make in a given time window.

title: Public baseline paragraph 17
text: Bearer tokens are sent in the Authorization header and should always travel over TLS.

title: Public baseline paragraph 18
text: Pagination with a cursor is more reliable than offset pagination when records are inserted while a client is reading.

title: Public baseline paragraph 19
text: Webhooks push event notifications to a customer-supplied URL instead of requiring the customer to poll.

title: Public baseline paragraph 20
text: Customer retention measures the share of customers who keep using a product over a period of time.

title: Public baseline paragraph 21
text: Cohort analysis groups customers by the month they signed up and tracks how each group behaves over time.

title: Public baseline paragraph 22
text: Net revenue retention includes expansion revenue from existing customers, so it can exceed one hundred percent.

title: Public baseline paragraph 23
text: Churn is the complement of retention: the share of customers who cancel or stop using the product in a period.

title: Public baseline paragraph 24
text: Data retention policies define how long logs and records are kept before they are archived or deleted.

title: Public baseline paragraph 25
text: Backups should be tested regularly by restoring them into a separate environment.

title: Public baseline paragraph 26
text: Service level objectives set a target for reliability, such as 99.9 percent of requests succeeding over thirty days.

title: Public baseline paragraph 27
text: An error budget is the amount of unreliability a service may consume before feature work pauses in favour of stability.

title: Public baseline paragraph 28
text: Observability combines metrics, logs and traces to explain why a system behaves the way it does.

title: Public baseline paragraph 29
text: Capacity planning estimates future load so that hardware and cloud resources are provisioned before they are needed.

title: Public baseline paragraph 30
text: Engineering teams often publish architecture decision records to explain why a design was chosen.
